notes: Inbound SMB — self-serve signup, small engineering team (5 engs).
Primary product: in-app chat assistant for support documentation (doc search + generative replies).
Customer complaint: "responses sometimes take 4-6s — kills UX on web widget". P95 ~800ms but P99 spikes to 4-6s during peak page loads.
Current setup: using hosted_api in us-east-1, model: redwood-small-v1 (default from catalog), single-threaded requests from frontend, no streaming enabled, no client-side timeout configured.
Traffic profile: low QPS (0.5–3 rps) but bursty from landing pages; typical request size 700-1,200 tokens (system + prompt + user_history).
Cost sensitivity: medium — wants to keep hosted plan and avoid Dedicated; estimated ARR target small so prefer self-serve pricing.
Security: requires SSO for admin console and audit logs, ok with public cloud hosting; data residency not strict (NA customers).

SE notes from trace: a) some requests routed to lower-cost fallback model due to transient capacity; b) client is not streaming and waits for full completion which increases observed latency; c) long system messages + full chat history included every request increasing token processing cost and latency.
Immediate triage recommendations provided to customer during call:
- Try region change test: send identical requests to us-west-2 to compare latency profile (frontend user base in west coast).
- Enable streaming responses for chat widget to improve perceived latency and allow token-level partial render.
- Implement short client-side timeout (e.g., 6s) with graceful fallback UI and retry to a cheaper model or show canned response.
- Trim system messages and limit conversation window: canonical guidance provided: keep system prompt <= 150 tokens, send last 2 user turns only, summarize older context server-side.
- Reduce max_tokens and set max_completion_tokens in generation call when using single-turn answers to cut tail latency.
- Use model routing: prefer low-latency 'redwood-lowlatency' variant for interactive traffic; fallback to 'redwood-small' for background jobs.
- Add route-level timeouts and instrumentation: set per-route 3s/6s thresholds and capture traces (request_id, region, model_variant) to linked support ticket INF-3124.

Customer reaction: positive to streaming and trimming prompts. Cautious about region flip — wants evidence before changing production. Quote: "If west coast cuts 2s off median we'll switch, but need a simple way to route users by geolocation."
Requested features / asks: region pinning in dashboard per-api-key, per-route timeout overrides, short perf checklist for low-QPS bursty apps (we provided a 1-page quickstart in Drive).
Potential upsell: if performance improves after tuning, customer may convert to paid hosted plan and add Redwood Optimize recommendations (cost saving + token trimming suggestions).
Risk: if UX doesn't improve quickly they will evaluate other hosted providers; vendor shortlist includes OpenAI and Anthropic for latency comparisons.
